name: Elephant-ear fish
summary: Cá tai tượng is the elephant-ear fish Vietnam Tourism’s dining chapter calls a classic Mekong plate: fried whole and rolled with pickles, cucumber, and herbs in rice paper. The chapter names Can Tho as a base. It does not say the dish was born in Can Tho.
origin: A Mekong plate in the dining chapter that uses Can Tho and Châu Đốc as bases. Not a Can Tho-only origin.
howToEat: Pulled off the upright fish and rolled in rice paper with pickles, cucumber, and herbs.
where: Mekong restaurants in that chapter. A Can Tho street was not named.
seoDescription: Fried whole and rolled in rice paper. Vietnam Tourism calls it a classic Mekong plate and names Can Tho as a base, not as the birthplace.
